title: B01 Direct competitor Indonesia selection and trial handoff
evidence_summary: The official page says the user receives a saveable profile covering symptoms, advice and Sensodyne product information, plus samples or coupons. This establishes an existing Indonesian mechanism connecting need clarification and trial. It does not establish that offers are currently fulfilled for every visitor, conversion rates, medical diagnosis or commercial effectiveness. Proposed differentiation must extend beyond a questionnaire and coupon. Relevant pillar: earned personal value. Verified page lines 94–107;
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B02 Direct competitor need-based navigation
evidence_summary: The live official site offers product matching and navigation by needs including whitening, gum health, cavity prevention, sensitivity, enamel, plaque and breath. This supports a simple need-led choice interface as feasible and already conventional. It supplies no observed conversion, repeat or cost benchmark and is an Indian portfolio. Relevant pillar: earned personal value.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B03 Pepsodent capabilities already in market
citation: Unilever Indonesia (2024), *AI Denta-Scan Lengkapi Layanan Konsultasi Gigi Online Tanya Dokter Gigi by Pepsodent*. https://www.unilever.co.id/news/press-releases/2024/ai-dentascan-lengkapi-layanan-konsultasi-gigi-online-tanya-dokter-gigi-by-pepsodent/
evidence_summary: The official release confirms AI Denta-Scan within Pepsodent's online dentist consultation and BKGN activities. This is an execution asset and an explicit prior-art check. It does not prove young-user Premium conversion or incremental profit. Reuse professional referral pathways when appropriate rather than manufacturing clinical authority inside a sales quiz. Relevant pillars: earned value and safe purchase enablement.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B04 Product truth and conditions
evidence_summary: The official page identifies a 100G product and named benefits, with a specific condition attached to its 30-second sensitivity claim: direct application and gentle finger massage on a sensitive tooth for 30 seconds. This is manufacturer product information, not an independent comparative trial. Do not copy an efficacy headline without its conditions. The strategy should use brand-approved claims and directions, make Basic acceptable when it meets the user's job, and avoid diagnosing pain. No current price or small trial SKU was confirmed here.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B05 Pepsodent whitening and existing scanner
evidence_summary: The official page lists Ultimate Bright, Fresh Shine, Gentle Radiance, Purified Shine and a spray, and links to Shade Scan AI. This confirms existing beauty-positioning, variant breadth and a digital shade tool. Testimonials are brand-hosted and are not independent consumer effectiveness evidence. Portfolio variant names do not authenticate an unclear survey answer or support coding every Pepsodent tube as Premium. Relevant pillar: earned personal value.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B06 Strong recent indirect trial-distribution benchmark
citation: Han, B. R., Chu, L. Y., Sun, T., & Wu, L. (online 10 December 2025). *Commercializing the Package Flow: Cross-Sampling Physical Products Through E-Commerce Warehouses*. Management Science. https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2020.00902
evidence_summary: A 2019 Alibaba quasi-experiment distributed 55,434 samples across six brands. Single-item buyers included 52,288 treated and 139,518 untreated customers; matching retained 41,566 in each group. The paper used difference-in-differences with matching. Campaign-month spending at the sampling brand rose by approximately 64% relative to control, equal to an estimated RMB0.218 per month; months 1–3 added RMB0.09 monthly. Store-visit probability increased 2.808 percentage points in month 0. Effects varied by prior behavior and matching. This supports testing efficient cross-category trial distribution. It does not imply a 64% toothpaste lift, Indonesian transferability, clinical value or lasting full-price repeat. Reporting the absolute spending changes prevents an inflated reading of the relative percentage.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B07 Recent evidence that channel changes the trial journey
citation: Paulich, B. J., Pansari, A., & Kumar, V. (2026). *Where did you receive the free sample? Sustained impact of new product sample distribution on customer purchase journey*. Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science, 54, 322–347. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11747-025-01123-3
evidence_summary: The publisher describes a randomized field experiment tracking engagement for 18 months. Online requests were cost-effective, direct mail produced the strongest long-term engagement, and in-store distribution had limited sustained engagement. The accessible abstract did not provide numerical effect sizes or enough operational detail to reproduce its economics. Use this as channel-design evidence, not a numeric conversion assumption. It cautions against optimizing sample handouts while ignoring use and later purchasing. Relevant pillars: earned value and replacement.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B08 Counterbenchmark sampling can fail
citation: Food Standards Agency, Gold, N., et al. (2024). *Exploring the impact of giving free food samples and loyalty cards on food choices: a stepped wedge trial in workplace food outlets*. FSA Research and Evidence. https://doi.org/10.46756/sci.fsa.paq622
evidence_summary: In 29 English workplace outlets, sampling plus loyalty cards did not significantly raise plant-based meal sales. The primary sampling-day coefficient was −0.53 meals per outlet-day, 95% CI −3.43 to 2.36, p=.718. Loyalty-card-only days were also nonsignificant. Three of 32 assigned sites dropped out; power limitations mean a small effect could be missed. This different product/category is an intentional counterexample: trial activity does not guarantee commercial change. Evaluate actual paid incremental conversion and contribution rather than samples distributed.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B09 Planning prompt randomized benchmark
citation: Milkman, K. L., Beshears, J., Choi, J. J., Laibson, D., & Madrian, B. C. (2011). *Using implementation intentions prompts to enhance influenza vaccination rates*. PNAS, 108(26), 10415–10420. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1103170108
evidence_summary: In a US workplace vaccination experiment of 3,272 eligible employees, all arms received clinic reminders. Arms contained 1,268 controls, 1,270 date-and-time planners and 734 date-only planners. Prompting employees to record a date and time increased vaccination by 4.2 percentage points over a 33.1% control rate, 95% CI 0.5–7.8, p=.03. Date-only planning added 1.5 points and was nonsignificant. This isolates specificity beyond reminder receipt and is useful for testing a concrete replenishment plan. It is an old, distant-category result involving eligible employees and free clinics, not a purchase elasticity, toothpaste effect, young-person estimate or budget assumption. Relevant pillar: secure replacement; secondary support for purchase handoff.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B10 Direct replenishment capability benchmark
citation: Oral-B US, *Frequently Asked Questions and Contact Us* (undated). https://oralb.com/en-us/faq-help-center/?page=resources
evidence_summary: The official site documents customer-selected automatic delivery schedules and options to skip a shipment, change dates and cancel. It establishes that controllable replenishment exists in oral care, but not Indonesian consumer demand, lower total price or published incremental retention. Brushes/refill heads have different depletion economics from shared toothpaste. Adapt the control principle through optional reminders and reorder links; do not infer that subscription or a fixed 30-day tube cycle is appropriate.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B11 Experimental availability benchmark
citation: Conlon, C. T., & Mortimer, J. H. (2010 working paper). *Effects of Product Availability: Experimental Evidence*. NBER Working Paper 16506. https://doi.org/10.3386/w16506
evidence_summary: Experiments removed top-selling products from vending machines and examined substitution and profits. The study found substantial substitution to alternatives and misaligned upstream/downstream stocking incentives. This supports measuring exact-SKU availability where people actually buy. No transferable toothpaste uplift is supplied. It does not prove that low survey stockout reports are false; reported search failure and latent shelf substitution are different phenomena. Partner-level retailer stock checks are needed before any stock availability claim. Relevant pillar: secure replacement.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B12 Shopping-list planning experiment and an important limit
citation: Davydenko, M., & Peetz, J. (2020). *Shopping less with shopping lists: Planning individual expenses ahead of time affects purchasing behavior when online grocery shopping*. Journal of Consumer Behaviour, 19(3), 240–251. https://doi.org/10.1002/cb.1812
evidence_summary: Two randomized studies examined making itemized lists before virtual grocery shopping. Lists reduced item purchasing, marginally in Study 1 and significantly in Study 2; a general spending prediction did not substitute for an itemized list. This supports externalizing an exact planned purchase, not the stronger claim that sharing a Premium toothpaste item with a parent increases acceptance. The latter is a project-specific hypothesis. No percentage uplift was extracted or should be fabricated. Relevant pillar: carry the choice into purchasing.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B13 Direct Pepsodent campaign feasibility with unsuitable commercial metrics
citation: InMobi, *Pepsodent Evokes Confident Merdeka Smiles with an AI-powered Brand Activation* (undated; archived campaign). https://advertising.inmobi.com/case-study/pepsodent-evokes-confident-merdeka-smiles-with-an-ai-powered-brand-activation
evidence_summary: The supplier describes family targeting, a mobile interaction and a buy-now handoff. Headline results are 14% higher video completion and 3.3x engagement, with comparators referenced by footnote markers but not disclosed in accessible page text. These are supplier-reported media metrics, not incremental Premium sales, sustained repeat or ROI. Use the case as proof that Pepsodent has previously connected family messaging to a buying route; do not use either number in the impact model.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B14 Shared household lists with item photos
evidence_summary: The official service supports lists shared with family and friends, synchronized changes and item photos intended to help the correct item get purchased. This is a clear direct functionality analogue for a user carrying an exact toothpaste choice into a household basket. It does not establish payer persuasion, Premium affordability or incremental conversion. The proposed service should use a shareable item through a familiar channel instead of requiring a new household app.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B15 Tier-neutral oral-care foundation
evidence_summary: The ADA states that toothpastes earning its cavity-protection seal must contain fluoride; additional ingredients can address other health or cosmetic functions. This supports separating foundational care from optional specialist benefits. It is a US professional information source, not an Indonesian product approval or endorsement of any Pepsodent SKU. Do not imply that Premium conversion itself improves health or that an unverified Basic formulation is inadequate.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast

title: B16 Regulatory boundary for advertising
citation: BPOM (2025), *BPOM Tegaskan Aturan Penandaan Promosi dan Iklan Kosmetik Wajib Dilaksanakan Pelaku Usaha*. https://www.pom.go.id/siaran-pers/bpom-tegaskan-aturan-penandaan-promosi-dan-iklan-kosmetik-wajib-dilaksanakan-pelaku-usaha
evidence_summary: The official clarification of PerBPOM 18/2024 says cosmetic advertising and testimonials may not be performed by health or medical professionals. Therefore a dentist must not act as a paid product demonstrator or testimonial in a toothpaste cosmetic sales execution. Product classification, educational/referral separation, and qualified claims need local compliance review before launch. The official Q&A further distinguishes educational discussion from cosmetic promotion. https://standar-otskk.pom.go.id/storage/uploads/b224faad-d5ad-4f78-ab79-f08ec8c75d87/Q-%26-A-Sosialisasi-PerBPOM-No.-18-tahun-2024.pdf .  This is an operational restriction, not legal sign-off for a specific campaign.
claim_scope: Mechanism benchmark only; not our forecast
